text:
The man is likely to prevail. When the woman conveyed the house to him, he owned both the dominant and servient parcels, so the easement was extinguished by merger. His later warranty deed didn't create a new easement, and the earlier easement isn't revived. An implied easement doesn't help the purchaser, because the path was never used while the man owned both parcels, and the facts suggest the purchaser had other access.

CONFIDENCE: 85
